evidence.publisher: Association for Computing Machinery and Association for Information Systems
evidence.title: IS 2020: A Competency Model for Undergraduate Programs in Information Systems
evidence.locator: Data/Information competency realm, pp. 2-3: database querying and design, programming database systems, database security, concurrency trade-offs and non-relational models; IT infrastructure realm, p. 4, includes infrastructure planning and enterprise architecture concepts.
evidence.supports: An independent academic competency framework corroborates database design/management and architecture/infrastructure as teachable competency areas relevant to a data-systems domain.

evidence.publisher: Association for Computing Machinery, Council on Education
evidence.title: Data Management (DM), Version Beta
evidence.locator: Preamble pp. 1-2 identifies data modeling/database design, query construction/processing and DBMS internals; p. 3 describes database architecture, transaction management, large-volume systems and distributed databases; pp. 10-12 list data-engineering/infrastructure roles and applied data-management competencies.
evidence.supports: An ACM computer-science curriculum proposal independently distinguishes modeling/design, database systems/operations, data engineering/infrastructure and data lifecycle competencies relevant to D002's engineering scope.

evidence.title: DAMA Guide to the Data Management Body of Knowledge (DAMA-DMBOK2R), 2nd edition revised
evidence.locator: Public context diagrams: Data Architecture; Data Modeling and Design; Data Storage and Operations; Data Integration and Interoperability; Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence; Metadata Management; Data Quality Management. DAMA's overview says the framework is a consensus-based foundation, not an exhaustive catalog or prescriptive standard.
evidence.supports: A global data-management professional framework distinguishes architecture/modeling, storage/operations, integration, warehousing, metadata and quality as established knowledge areas relevant to D002's stated scope.

evidence.locator: Eight knowledge domains: Security and Risk Management; Asset Security; Security Architecture and Engineering; Communication and Network Security; Identity and Access Management; Security Assessment and Testing; Security Operations; Software Development Security. evidence.supports: An internationally offered professional certification body treats governance/risk, architecture, networks, identity, testing, operations and secure development as substantial distinguishable cybersecurity knowledge domains.

evidence.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology, NICE initiative
evidence.title: NICE Cybersecurity Workforce Framework (NIST SP 800-181 overview)

evidence.supports: There are distinct concentrated cybersecurity work functions, including governance, defense, analysis/investigation, operations and secure provisioning. This is particularly relevant to defining area-of-specialization boundaries.

evidence.title: Platform Engineering Maturity Model
evidence.locator: Sections 'What is platform engineering?' and 'How to use this model', lines 14-27 of the web edition: platform engineering plans and provides computing platforms; its aspects are independently evaluated and implementations vary by organization.
evidence.supports: Independent CNCF elaboration that platform engineering is a coherent specialization area and that platform implementations are contextual rather than a rigid universal checklist.

evidence.publisher: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), Platforms Working Group and TAG App Delivery contributors
evidence.title: Platforms White Paper for Cloud Native Computing
evidence.locator: Overview and linked white paper: internal platforms provide common capabilities and services to application/product teams; the paper addresses platform capabilities, outcomes, measurement and platform-team success.
evidence.supports: Platform engineering is a distinct cloud-native practice area focused on providing reusable internal capabilities and developer-facing platform services, rather than a synonym for infrastructure operations or all DevOps work.

evidence.title: FinOps Framework Phases
evidence.locator: Inform, Optimize and Operate phases, especially lines 101-131 of the web edition: technology cost/usage visibility, optimization, and collaborative action across engineering, finance and business teams.
evidence.supports: Cloud cost/usage optimization is an important capability connected to cloud engineering and operation.

evidence.title: What is Site Reliability Engineering?
evidence.locator: 'What is Site Reliability Engineering?' and 'What we do as SRE' sections: reliability work applies software engineering to operations and focuses on availability, latency, performance, capacity, and running production systems.
evidence.supports: Cloud service reliability and production operations are a recognizable, task-distinct area, not merely another name for building infrastructure or authoring deployment pipelines.

evidence.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
evidence.title: NIST Cloud Computing Reference Architecture
evidence.locator: Section 2.1, printed pp. 3-4 / PDF pp. 9-10, identifies cloud consumer, provider, carrier, auditor and broker actors; Appendix A, printed pp. 20-21 / PDF pp. 26-27, defines SaaS, PaaS and IaaS. Section 3 describes provider-side service orchestration, resource abstraction/control, physical resources and service management.
evidence.supports: Cloud architecture, infrastructure/service provision, and cloud service operations are materially different concerns; IaaS/PaaS/SaaS are service models and the actor taxonomy is a reference architecture, not learner specialization labels.

domains.domain_name: Internet of Things and Embedded Systems

areas.label: Embedded Systems and Firmware Engineering
areas.boundary: Design and implement software that runs close to device hardware, including microcontroller-based systems, hardware interfaces, constrained resources, timing behavior, and device-level testing.

evidence.title: Arm Keil MDK Getting Started Guide, software components in CMSIS-Packs
evidence.locator: Section 5, 'Software components in CMSIS-Packs': describes embedded software as modular systems built from components such as middleware, source code, libraries and example projects targeted to microcontroller families/platforms.
evidence.supports: Microcontroller/embedded firmware development is a coherent device-level technical area with its own platform and component constraints, distinct from integrating complete networked IoT systems.

evidence.publisher: European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI), with IoT/edge standards community contributors
evidence.title: Enabling Multi-access Edge Computing in the IoT: How to deploy ETSI MEC and oneM2M
evidence.locator: Introduction and Figure 1, printed pp. 4-5: distinguishes IoT devices/things, edge nodes/network edge, core network and cloud data center; describes moving compute/data hosting toward the edge for latency and bandwidth needs. The paper's objective is to connect ETSI MEC and oneM2M standardization/deployment concerns.
evidence.supports: Edge computing is a distinct systems-design concern about where compute and data hosting occur and how edge services interoperate with IoT architectures; it is not just another name for embedded firmware or IoT architecture as a whole.

evidence.publisher: International Organization for Standardization and International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 41)
evidence.title: ISO/IEC 30141:2024 Internet of Things (IoT) � Reference architecture
evidence.locator: ISO's public abstract and edition information; the 2024 second edition describes a standardized IoT reference architecture with a common vocabulary, reusable designs and implementation patterns. Public online table of contents for the edition lists foundational, business, usage, functional, trustworthiness and construction viewpoints, plus construction patterns.
evidence.supports: IoT system architecture is a distinct design concern involving multiple viewpoints and construction patterns, not simply device programming or a list of application sectors.

evidence.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Cyber-Physical Systems Public Working Group
evidence.title: Framework for Cyber-Physical Systems: Volume 1, Overview (NIST SP 1500-201)
evidence.locator: Abstract and framework summary: CPS joins interacting digital, analog, physical and human components; engineering facets are conceptualization, realization and assurance; concerns include functional behavior, trustworthiness, timing, data, composition, boundaries and lifecycle. Identifies application sectors separately from engineering concerns.
evidence.supports: Embedded/CPS engineering has device/physical-system constraints and lifecycle/assurance concerns that are not reducible to IoT service integration. Sector labels are applications, not necessarily specialization areas.

evidence.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
evidence.title: NIST SP 800-183, Networks of 'Things'
evidence.locator: NIST publication abstract: identifies sensing, computing, communication and actuation as core primitives of IoT/network-of-things systems; applies to distributed systems with scale, heterogeneity, temporal, reliability and security concerns.
evidence.supports: IoT spans interacting device and network functions; sensing/actuation are system functions and should not be confused with a complete learner specialization by themselves.

evidence.publisher: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) and IEEE Computer Society
evidence.title: CS2013 Knowledge Area: Human-Computer Interaction
evidence.locator: HCI overview and units HCI/Foundations, HCI/Designing Interaction, and HCI/User-Centered Design & Testing. The user-centered unit includes needs gathering, prototyping, evaluation with/without users, and reporting.
evidence.supports: Independent earlier curriculum framework corroborates the distinction between interaction design and user-centered research/testing/evaluation.

evidence.publisher: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) and IEEE Computer Society curriculum task force
evidence.title: Computing Curricula 2023 � Human-Computer Interaction Core
evidence.locator: HCI-A Understanding the User (needs-finding and user-centered methods); HCI-C Accessibility and Inclusive Design; HCI-D Evaluating the Design; HCI-E System Design and prototyping. The page states these are HCI knowledge units in a computing curriculum.
evidence.supports: User research/understanding, evaluation, interaction/system design, and accessibility/inclusive design are recognized as distinguishable HCI knowledge areas. This provides an international academic basis for separating the proposed branches.

evidence.title: ISO 9241-210:2019 Ergonomics of human-system interaction � Part 210: Human-centred design for interactive systems
evidence.locator: Public abstract and status page: requirements/recommendations for human-centred design principles and activities through the lifecycle of interactive systems; intended for process managers and human-factors/usability professionals. Page confirms 2019 edition remains current after 2025 review.
evidence.supports: Human-centred design is a lifecycle practice with user and usability concerns broader than visual UI production alone.

evidence.title: About the Usability Body of Knowledge
evidence.locator: Mission and project description: a living, broad and inclusive reference for usability practice, intended to collate published literature, conference proceedings and practitioner knowledge; the organization notes the field is multidisciplinary.
evidence.supports: Usability/user-experience practice is broad and multidisciplinary; research, design and evaluation may be distinct but connected activities.

areas.label: BI Data Foundations and Architecture
areas.boundary: Model, integrate, quality-check and organize organizational data for reliable analytical use; design and maintain warehouses, marts, semantic structures, metadata and appropriate access/governance foundations.

evidence.publisher: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) and Association for Information Systems (AIS)
evidence.title: IS 2010 Curriculum Guidelines for Undergraduate Degree Programs in Information Systems
evidence.locator: Data, Information and Knowledge Management material: data quality, OLTP versus OLAP, business intelligence, data warehousing and data mining; includes learning outcomes for creating a simple data warehouse/data mart and explaining the relationship among these concepts.
evidence.supports: Separates the BI information foundation (warehouse/OLAP) from analytic use/mining and situates both in organizational information systems.

evidence.title: DAMA-DMBOK 2.0 Revised: Infographics / Knowledge Areas
evidence.locator: Knowledge-area map lists Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence separately from Data Architecture, Data Modeling and Design, Data Storage and Operations, Data Integration and Interoperability, Metadata Management and Data Quality Management.
evidence.supports: BI has an identifiable professional knowledge area connected to, but not identical with, architecture, integration, modeling, storage and quality practices.

evidence.title: DAMA-DMBOK Revision
evidence.locator: 2024 revision description: maintenance release; overarching data-management framework and knowledge areas retained, with terminology/structure clarifications.
evidence.supports: Confirms the DMBOK knowledge-area framework remains maintained and that BI sits within a broader data-management ecosystem.

evidence.title: TDWI Analytics Maturity Model Assessment
evidence.locator: Assessment description: analytics deployments mature beyond spreadsheets/dashboards toward self-service and organizational capability; the framework assesses analytics-program dimensions and decision/use of analytics.
evidence.supports: Distinguishes BI delivery/reporting from broader organizational analytics capability and its use in decisions.

evidence.publisher: Transforming Data With Intelligence (TDWI), in partnership with the Institute for Certification of Computing Professionals (ICCP)
evidence.title: Overview of the Certified Business Intelligence Professional Certification
evidence.locator: CBIP scope lists BI (dashboards, reporting, visualization), analytics, data management (modeling, quality, integration), data architecture (warehouse/marts/lakes/metadata), and strategy/program methods. The guide is described as the basis for examination scope.
evidence.supports: Professional BI practice spans reporting/visualization, data foundations, analytics and program strategy, corroborating the need for distinct but connected areas.

areas.label: Quantitative Pricing and Financial Engineering
areas.boundary: Use mathematical and computational models to value financial instruments and engineer financial products/strategies, including derivative valuation, numerical methods, calibration and model implementation.

evidence.title: CFA Program Candidate Body of Knowledge
evidence.locator: Quantitative Methods includes probability, regression, time series, AI/ML and big-data applications, backtesting/simulation/scenario analysis; portfolio topics include construction, execution, trading and market microstructure.
evidence.supports: Quantitative methods are used in investment analysis and portfolio decisions; systematic investment, execution and market microstructure form distinguishable applied concerns.

evidence.title: Portfolio Mathematics (2026 Curriculum)
evidence.locator: Learning outcomes cover expected portfolio value, variance, standard deviation, covariance/correlation and shortfall-risk metrics; the reading connects quantitative portfolio mathematics to portfolio risk/return.
evidence.supports: Quantitative portfolio measurement and risk analysis are core, identifiable financial applications of mathematical methods.

evidence.title: CFA Program Curriculum Overview
evidence.locator: Curriculum structures quantitative methods, derivatives/risk management, portfolio construction, asset classes and specialized portfolio-management pathways as distinct topic areas.
evidence.supports: Financial valuation/risk and portfolio decision-making are related but distinguishable knowledge/application clusters.

evidence.title: Active Equity Investing: Strategies (2026 Curriculum)
evidence.locator: Summary and learning outcomes distinguish quantitative/systematic from fundamental/discretionary investing; describes factor, statistical-arbitrage and market-microstructure strategies, and quantitative workflow including data processing, backtesting, evaluation, portfolio construction, risk and trading-cost models.
evidence.supports: Systematic quantitative investment/trading is a coherent application area distinct from general financial modeling and risk quantification.

evidence.title: FRM Program Exams and Topic Areas

evidence.supports: Quantitative methods and valuation models form a distinct foundation, with applied financial risk areas such as market, credit and liquidity risk; professional material also connects risk and investment management.

open_items: Professional registration and planning law are jurisdiction-specific. Global discipline boundaries should be retained while local licensing and statutory practice are explicitly labelled.

Surveying, geomatics, cartography, landscape architecture, mobility planning and building inspection are present in the current D021 role set and need task-level parent-domain dispositions; some may belong under other existing or newly clarified roots.

disposition.label: rename/merge/split/add/remove specialization areas
disposition.reason: The checked academic/professional curriculum evidence now supports a domain-level specialization structure; the earlier deferral was not dependent on the later role-fit audit.

domains.recommendation_text: Two learner-facing branches are evidenced directly by a university clinical-informatics specialization and a separate public-health-informatics track. Health data standards, interoperability, analytics and architecture remain cross-cutting content in this evidence set rather than a third standalone route; this avoids converting WHO system/application types or IMIA knowledge domains into specializations. This is a defensible internal taxonomy, not an exhaustive global standard.
domains.count_rationale: Two learner-facing branches are evidenced directly by a university clinical-informatics specialization and a separate public-health-informatics track. Health data standards, interoperability, analytics and architecture remain cross-cutting content in this evidence set rather than a third standalone route; this avoids converting WHO system/application types or IMIA knowledge domains into specializations. This is a defensible internal taxonomy, not an exhaustive global standard.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Two learner-facing branches are evidenced directly by a university clinical-informatics specialization and a separate public-health-informatics track. Health data standards, interoperability, analytics and architecture remain cross-cutting content in this evidence set rather than a third standalone route; this avoids converting WHO system/application types or IMIA knowledge domains into specializations. This is a defensible internal taxonomy, not an exhaustive global standard.
defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.alternatives_considered: Reject the current four buckets because they mix generic occupational classifications and technology/system functions. Reject five WHO architecture types as specializations because WHO defines them as system/application types. Do not add a third health-data-systems specialization without comparative curricula showing it is an additive learner route rather than shared technical content.
defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.boundary_or_exclusion_rules: Use the recorded area boundaries. Cross-cutting competencies, technologies, system types, supervisory topics, and modalities stay within relevant learning paths unless independent education evidence establishes a distinct learner route.
defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.explicit_non_decisions: No role-to-specialization assignment, role/ISCO membership inference, national-context addition, or canonical taxonomy edit is made in this Step 1 reconciliation.

domains.recommendation_text: Recommend two broad student-facing areas as an internal synthesis: (1) Spacecraft and Payload Systems Engineering; (2) Ground Systems, Space Communications and Mission Operations. domains.count_rationale: source-supported internal synthesis; NASA/ESA/ISO establish distinct engineering system contexts and learning components, but no source prescribes exactly two student specializations

alternatives_considered: Use space, ground and user segments as three specializations: rejected because they are end-to-end architecture partitions; user/application work is often a downstream discipline and the architecture does not claim these are educational specializations.

Create separate subgroups for each spacecraft subsystem (propulsion, power, thermal, avionics, GNC, payload): rejected for this layer because these are nested engineering disciplines/topics within spacecraft and payload systems and would over-fragment the student-facing taxonomy.

Flatten the entire domain: not preferred because primary mission-engineering material distinguishes spacecraft/flight systems from ground infrastructure and mission operations, which entail different system responsibilities and learning additions.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the three inherited occupational buckets with six candidate learning areas: Economic Research, Econometrics and Forecasting; Computational Economics and Economic Modelling; Public Economics, Policy and Evaluation; Macroeconomic, Monetary and Financial Economics; International, Trade and Development Economics; and Applied Sector Economics. The sixth area should expose sector themes (industrial/innovation, labour/demographic, health/education/welfare, agricultural/environmental, urban/regional) rather than silently treating every JEL subfield as a separate card. Computational Economics is named explicitly because it has a recognized methods community and dedicated university curricula, although its methods also support other areas. This is a provisional synthesis, not an externally mandated six-area taxonomy.
domains.count_rationale: Six is a practical candidate synthesis of the broad root scope: it makes computational economics visible and groups the extensive AEA sector classifications into an applied-sector umbrella. It is not derived from the current three subgroup records or the number of roles. The applied-sector umbrella is a deliberate usability compromise and should be checked against the complete catalogue and user-facing card density; an alternative is a larger set that separates labour, health/education, industrial/innovation, environmental/agricultural, and regional economics.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Six is a practical candidate synthesis of the broad root scope: it makes computational economics visible and groups the extensive AEA sector classifications into an applied-sector umbrella. It is not derived from the current three subgroup records or the number of roles. The applied-sector umbrella is a deliberate usability compromise and should be checked against the complete catalogue and user-facing card density; an alternative is a larger set that separates labour, health/education, industrial/innovation, environmental/agricultural, and regional economics.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep the current three groups, including Teaching Professionals, as the student-facing areas
alternatives_considered.reason: The labels mix an unrelated occupational family with broad policy and research clusters and do not represent the recognized breadth of economics subject areas or the explicitly documented computational route.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Treat all quantitative/computational skills as only one generic economic-research area
alternatives_considered.reason: The Society for Computational Economics and multiple university curricula distinguish programming, numerical methods, simulation, optimization and computational modeling as coherent economic learning content. Name that route while allowing its methods to support other branches.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a separate student card for every AEA JEL field or code family
alternatives_considered.reason: JEL is a scholarly indexing classification, not a student pathway standard. Many fields share foundations and would create excessive fragmentation; sector-specific themes can be exposed inside an applied-economics path until separate routes are justified.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep all financial economics under D063 without boundary review
alternatives_considered.reason: JEL recognizes financial economics within economics, but the product catalogue has separate quantitative-finance, investment-analysis and trading domains. Clarify the economic-analysis portion versus finance practice to prevent duplicate or contradictory routes.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Make D063 a flat domain with no specializations
alternatives_considered.reason: The evidence shows materially distinct subject areas and methods with different learning outputs. A flat view would obscure these routes; however, the exact number and grouping remain provisional.

residual_uncertainties: AEA JEL is a scholarly classification for indexing economics literature, not an accreditation standard or mandated learning-path taxonomy.
The Society for Computational Economics is an international scholarly/professional society; its descriptions establish a recognized methods field, not a licensing or employment requirement.

OECD evaluation criteria are an international policy framework, originally for development cooperation and now used more broadly; their use still depends on context and is not a universal economics curriculum.
World Bank DIME is an institutional impact-evaluation programme; it evidences applied evaluation practice but is not a global occupational standard.

Southampton, Edinburgh and McGill are institution-specific curricula in the UK and Canada. Their course structures corroborate computational learning content but do not prescribe a universal sequence.
The six-area count and grouping, especially the Applied and Sector Economics umbrella, are a reasoned proposal. Full catalogue-boundary review and external academic feedback remain outstanding.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the four occupational buckets with nine candidate student-facing areas: Clinical Psychology; Clinical Neuropsychology; Counselling Psychology and Psychotherapy; Educational, School and Developmental Psychology; Health Psychology; Community Psychology; Forensic Psychology; Work and Organizational Psychology; and Sport and Exercise Psychology. Treat research, assessment and measurement as cross-cutting capabilities rather than a standalone specialization card. This nine-area proposal is an internal synthesis of recurring areas in official US, UK and Australian professional recognition structures; those bodies do not prescribe a common international count or identical title boundaries.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the four occupation-derived buckets with six candidate learning areas: Translation, Localization and Transcreation; Interpreting; Terminology and Language-Services Project Practice; Linguistic Research, Description and Documentation; Applied Linguistics and Language Learning; Computational Linguistics and Language Technology. Treat legal/medical/literary/technical texts, language pairs, interpreting modes, and sign-language modality as contextual pathways or themes unless separate evidence supports an independent, complete learning route. The count is an internal synthesis, not a global standard.
domains.count_rationale: Six is a compact synthesis that makes the combined parent’s professional-service, disciplinary, applied and computational directions visible. Sources do not prescribe six. A smaller alternative would merge terminology into language services and computational linguistics into research; a larger alternative would split linguistics subfields and legal/health/conference/signed interpreting. The recommended middle grouping should be checked against display density and available downstream content.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Six is a compact synthesis that makes the combined parent’s professional-service, disciplinary, applied and computational directions visible. Sources do not prescribe six. A smaller alternative would merge terminology into language services and computational linguistics into research; a larger alternative would split linguistics subfields and legal/health/conference/signed interpreting. The recommended middle grouping should be checked against display density and available downstream content.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Retain the four current ISCO family labels as student specializations
alternatives_considered.reason: They group occupations by broad code families, not by coherent language-service or linguistics learning areas.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a separate specialization for every subject matter translated (legal, medical, literary, technical, etc.)
alternatives_considered.reason: FIT and CIOL identify these as translation text sectors or contexts, but a subject label alone does not show a complete separate language-learning pathway; keep contextual tracks unless source curricula demonstrate otherwise.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a separate subgroup for every interpreting venue or modality
alternatives_considered.reason: Conference, public-service, legal, health and signed-language practice can differ substantially, but regulation and terminology vary regionally. Represent nested tracks first and split only when distinct learning additions and source support are documented.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Omit computational linguistics because the existing computational scanner has only one hit
alternatives_considered.reason: The scanner is not the authority. ACL provides direct international field evidence for computational linguistics/NLP, so the specialization is supported independently of the single lexical hit.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Treat all language technology and machine translation as human translation specializations
alternatives_considered.reason: Computational language modelling/system development has different learning outcomes from human translation. Show interoperable but distinct routes and do not imply machines replace professional judgement.

residual_uncertainties: FIT is an international federation of member associations; its position papers and descriptions support globally recognized language-service activities but do not create a single global certification or regulator.
CIOL qualifications and the DPSI are UK-regulated/nationally scoped even when candidates sit internationally; do not present them as universal requirements.
ACL is an international scientific/professional society; computational linguistics is established, but role titles and curricula vary across employers and institutions.
LSA proceedings are peer-reviewed scholarly outlets and the cited review/scope sources are not a universal accreditation taxonomy.

The exact six-area synthesis and the scope of the umbrella applied-linguistics and language-services areas remain internal recommendations; complete cross-domain and student-display review is outstanding.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the three mixed occupation/level buckets with eight candidate areas: Companion Animal Medicine and Surgery; Equine Medicine and Surgery; Livestock, Poultry and Aquatic Animal Health and Production; Veterinary Public Health, Food Safety and Epidemiology; Veterinary Clinical Disciplines and Diagnostics; Wildlife, Zoo and Conservation Medicine; Animal Welfare, Behaviour and Clinical Nutrition; Laboratory Animal Science and Veterinary Research. These combine recurring species/context groupings and cross-species disciplines appearing in WOAH international veterinary-education material and the RCVS specialist framework. The count is an internal synthesis, not a global accreditation taxonomy; retain cross-cutting specialties as skills/paths shared across species where appropriate.
domains.count_rationale: Eight is a compact internal synthesis of the international competency breadth and the UK specialist groups; it is not a count prescribed by either source. RCVS lists many more narrow specialty titles, which are too granular for root-level cards; WOAH describes core competency domains rather than specialty labels. The proposed count should be checked against the full programme and display catalogue, especially whether equine merits a separate card globally and whether welfare/behaviour/nutrition should split.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Eight is a compact internal synthesis of the international competency breadth and the UK specialist groups; it is not a count prescribed by either source. RCVS lists many more narrow specialty titles, which are too granular for root-level cards; WOAH describes core competency domains rather than specialty labels. The proposed count should be checked against the full programme and display catalogue, especially whether equine merits a separate card globally and whether welfare/behaviour/nutrition should split.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep Veterinarians and Animal Therapists / Veterinary Nurses and Technicians as specializations
alternatives_considered.reason: These labels split by occupation and qualification level rather than by an area of veterinary science. Learners need the veterinary subject/context areas; role qualification routes are separate.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a subgroup for every RCVS recognized specialty and subspecialty
alternatives_considered.reason: The RCVS list contains many advanced titles and nested subspecialties under UK recognition rules. These should become deeper routes or item tags, not dozens of root-level specialization cards.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Combine all species areas into one general veterinary clinical area
alternatives_considered.reason: WOAH and RCVS materials distinguish production animals, companion/competitive animals, aquatic, equine and wildlife contexts with materially different populations and practice settings.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Add a separate computational veterinary specialization from scanner hits
alternatives_considered.reason: The three scanner hits concern quantitative tasks in existing competencies. Veterinary epidemiology, surveillance, diagnostics and research can use data/modelling, but current evidence does not establish a separate global computational-veterinary specialization. Treat computational methods as evidence-linked themes until a fuller international curriculum audit supports a distinct route.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Split Veterinary Public Health from Food Safety and Epidemiology
alternatives_considered.reason: These are strongly connected through veterinary surveillance, zoonoses, veterinary services and food hygiene/safety. Separate cards could be warranted if they have distinct learning additions and source-backed routes in the full catalogue.

residual_uncertainties: WOAH/OIE veterinary-education materials are international guidance for competencies and curriculum development; they are not a global accreditation syllabus or an exact specialty taxonomy.
RCVS specialty titles, registration and use of 'specialist' are UK-specific. The RCVS taxonomy informs candidate subject boundaries, not globally portable legal status.
Species and specialist recognition vary across national/regional veterinary education and regulatory systems; country-specific qualifications, permits and service authorities must be labelled.
The eight-area count is an internal synthesis. Equine split, public health grouping, and the combination of welfare/behaviour/nutrition remain review points.
This review does not assess veterinary nursing/technician scope, role-domain fit, role-specialization fit, or the necessary educational/legal qualification level for any occupation.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the three occupation-family labels at the specialization layer with eight broad practice areas: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery; Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics; Pediatric and Special Care Dentistry; Endodontics; Periodontology; Prosthodontics and Implant Dentistry; Oral Medicine, Diagnosis and Orofacial Pain; and Dental Public Health. These are learning-area groupings, not a claim that each is formally recognized or separately licensed in every country. Keep a shared foundational dentistry layer before these advanced routes.

domains.recommendation_text: Provisionally organize civil-aviation learning into seven candidate areas: Flight Operations and Aircrew; Air Traffic Management and Air Navigation; Aircraft Maintenance and Continuing Airworthiness; Airport, Airline and Ground Operations; Aviation Safety Management; Aviation Security and Facilitation; and Uncrewed Aircraft Systems and Remote Operations. Keep cabin safety/service within flight operations unless the full learning contract supports a distinct branch; keep aeronautical information services within air navigation. Do not add aerospace design or computational aerodynamics to this operational taxonomy until the parent-domain boundary is resolved.
domains.count_rationale: Source-grounded internal synthesis of internationally recognized aviation system functions; no source prescribes exactly seven learner-facing areas.

domains.recommendation_text: Use six provisional areas: Theatre and Dramatic Performance; Music Performance and Creation; Dance and Choreography; Opera and Music Theatre; Circus and Physical Performance; and Live Performance Production and Technical Theatre. Keep presenters, conductors, stage managers, designers and technical disciplines within the relevant practice area or production route rather than treating occupation titles as areas. Treat festivals/markets as a presenting and distribution context, not a learner specialization by default. Resolve screen/recorded-media ownership before canonical implementation.

Treat research methods as shared foundations plus methods added within each discipline; the computational area is a genuine cross-cutting specialization supported by digital sociology, not a claim that all social-science roles require programming. This route can use theory, interviews, observation, documents or other evidence to explain patterns in social life. It is not a claim that one course or one study can describe every community, and it does not replace any professional licence or specialist training.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the excluded occupational bucket with three candidate areas of specialization: Retail Sales and Customer Experience; Retail Merchandising and Category Management; and Retail Store and Omnichannel Operations. This is a concise internal synthesis of international retail process and vocational task evidence, not an APQC/WorldSkills/ILO-mandated taxonomy. Omnichannel/e-commerce is treated as a cross-cutting channel context, not a standalone area. This does not approve or assign any role.
domains.count_rationale: source_reviewed_specialization_set_recommended

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Three is the smallest defensible synthesis of the independently visible customer-facing, merchandising/product-planning, and store/channel-operation clusters. A separate e-commerce subgroup was not added because the global retail framework treats channels as a connected capability and the ILO describes online versus physical as a channel distinction; technology/channel use can occur across sales, customer experience and operations. Product-category seller titles are role/product contexts, not separate specialization areas.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep the single 'Sales Workers' subgroup as the student-facing area
alternatives_considered.reason: It is an excluded ISCO occupational grouping rather than an audited, student-facing retail specialization and combines materially different task clusters.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a separate E-commerce/Omnichannel specialization
alternatives_considered.reason: The reviewed global sources support digital and physical channels, but channel is cross-cutting across customer experience, selling and store operations. The evidence reviewed does not establish a distinct D085 learning specialization with a boundary cleanly separate from those areas. Revisit if additional international retail professional frameworks establish such a distinct specialization.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create separate specialization groups for every product category or seller title
alternatives_considered.reason: Product category is a context for specialized selling, not evidence of a distinct retail work area; it would fragment the taxonomy and make subgroup count follow role-title volume.

residual_uncertainties: APQC is an industry process framework and WorldSkills is a vocational benchmark; neither is an academic accreditation body or prescriptive specialization taxonomy. The three labels and their count are an internal synthesis requiring eventual external academic review if formal endorsement is desired.

The repository domain title includes shop operations but its role inventory has 70 ISCO-52 records, including rental/leasing and other possible cross-domain cases. The parallel role audit may find that records do not fit D085; role volume must not determine subgroup count.

Retail inventory, customer relations, marketing and digital commerce overlap with logistics, marketing and technology domains. Keep only retail-specific work within D085 and assess each role/task independently.

Canonical implementation remains pending independent specialization identifiers and compatible seed/API support; this recommendation does not change canonical role membership or approve any role assignment.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the four ISCO-derived visible groups with four candidate, gaming-specific specialization areas: Casino and Venue Gaming Operations; Betting and Wagering Operations; Lottery, Bingo and Draw-Based Operations; and Gaming Products and Systems. This is an internal synthesis of international gaming-sector operational and technical standards, not a WLA/GLI-mandated academic taxonomy. Responsible-gaming, compliance, integrity and security principles are cross-cutting obligations, not a separate specialization solely because standards treat them as important. No role assignment or role-domain approval is made.
domains.count_rationale: source_reviewed_specialization_set_recommended

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Four areas are a provisional minimum that distinguishes three different game-operation contexts from a fourth technical/product lifecycle context supported by both standards sources. A separate subgroup for online gaming is not added because online delivery is a channel across lottery, casino and betting products. Separate compliance/security/ responsible-gaming groups are not added because the standards describe them as cross-cutting control obligations, not necessarily distinct specializations. The current 13-role distribution is not used to justify the count.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep the four current active ISCO-major buckets as the specialization list
alternatives_considered.reason: They group roles by broad occupational classification, not by gaming-industry practice. They mix customer-service, management and technical occupations without explaining gaming-specific study areas or justifying fit.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create one subgroup for every game format (casino, poker, slots, bingo, keno, lottery, raffles, sportsbook, esports, horse racing, online games)
alternatives_considered.reason: The standards distinguish product types, but many are formats/channels within shared operations. A subgroup per format would fragment the student taxonomy; retain them as examples within the four evidenced areas unless later curriculum and professional sources demonstrate distinct learning specializations.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create Compliance and Responsible Gaming as a fifth specialization
alternatives_considered.reason: WLA controls and responsible-gaming principles establish these as important, cross-cutting operator obligations. That evidence alone does not establish an independent student-facing specialization within D086; assess compliance roles against the parent domain and consider adjacent domain links separately.

residual_uncertainties: The WLA standard focuses on security/integrity controls and GLI on technical system testing; neither is an academic framework. The four areas are an internal synthesis and not externally accredited or endorsed.

The domain title says 'operations', while some current roles describe game development, quality assurance and information-security leadership. The separate role audit may conclude that some are better placed in software engineering, cybersecurity, compliance or another domain, with D086 retained only as a supported context/adjacency where warranted.
Gaming regulation, permitted products, licensing and required credentials vary by jurisdiction. No jurisdiction-specific authorization or certification is generalized as a global student requirement.
Canonical implementation remains pending specialization identifiers independent of ISCO and compatible seed/API support.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the excluded ISCO bucket with three candidate student-facing areas: Barbering and Facial-Hair Grooming; Haircutting, Styling and Colour Services; and Wigs, Extensions and Hair Replacement. This is a compact internal synthesis of international vocational standards and comparative occupational task profiles, not a WorldSkills/O*NET/UK-NOS-mandated taxonomy. It makes no decision about whether any of the five current roles fits D087 or any candidate area.
domains.count_rationale: source_reviewed_specialization_set_recommended

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Three is the smallest useful synthesis supported by the evidence: a barbering/facial-hair cluster; core hair design and treatment services (including colourist as a recognizable specialty within this area); and a distinct hairpiece/extension/replacement technical cluster. Do not add a separate subgroup for every hair type, gender, chemical technique, occasion or production channel; those are client contexts, techniques or cross-cutting settings unless further global curricular evidence establishes an independent specialization.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep Personal Services Workers as the student-facing specialization
alternatives_considered.reason: It is an excluded ISCO occupation grouping, not a hair-practice area, and combines personal service roles without explaining which hair knowledge or services distinguish them.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create colourist as a separate fourth area
alternatives_considered.reason: WorldSkills and UK occupational standards recognize colour as a distinct technical competency and a possible specialization; the current evidence does not show it needs a separate top-level student branch instead of a focused track within Haircutting, Styling and Colour Services. Revisit if cross-regional curricula establish a distinct standalone route.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create separate specializations for wigs, extensions, film/theatre hair, and hair replacement
alternatives_considered.reason: The sources support a shared specialist technical core in selecting, fitting, styling, maintaining and removing hairpieces/extensions, while film/theatre is a work setting. Keep production design as context and allow supported cross-domain links rather than fragmenting the top-level taxonomy.

residual_uncertainties: The evidence combines an international vocational benchmark with U.S. and UK occupational sources. It supports candidate work-area boundaries, but does not substitute for cross-regional academic consultation or establish universal licensing/qualification requirements.

Hair replacement may include medical, prosthetic or dermatological contexts beyond ordinary hair services; those boundaries require role-task assessment and, where relevant, health-professional scope-of-practice review.
Canonical implementation remains pending specialization identifiers independent of ISCO and compatible seed/API support.

evidence.claim_supported: A separately classified barber occupation has a recognizable task emphasis in hair cutting and shaving/facial-hair services, corroborating a distinct barbering practice area within personal hair services.
evidence.claim_limit: O*NET is a U.S. occupational dataset, not an international taxonomy or academic accreditation source. Use it as comparative task evidence only; local titles and licensing vary. It cannot validate D087 role mappings by itself. Geographic scope: United States.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the excluded ISCO bucket with six candidate areas: Facial Skincare and Non-medical Aesthetics; Body Therapy and Massage; Spa Therapy and Wellness Services; Nail Care and Enhancement; Hair Removal and Epilation; and Make-up, Brow and Lash Artistry. This is an internal synthesis of WorldSkills' international occupational standard, CIDESCO's international qualification portfolio and UK occupational competency standards. It is not a mandated six-part taxonomy, an academic accreditation decision, or a role-fit decision. Medical aesthetics, clinical skincare and weight-loss treatment remain outside absent appropriate regulated scope and evidence.
domains.count_rationale: source_reviewed_specialization_set_recommended

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Six is a provisional minimal synthesis matching the independently described service clusters and the domain's explicit beauty/aesthetics/spa scope, while keeping nail, epilation and make-up practices visible rather than burying them in a generic 'beauty' bucket. Spa therapy is retained as its own pathway because CIDESCO defines it as standalone, but spa is not treated as a venue-based duplicate of facial/body services. Aromatherapy is treated as a method used across areas, not a separate top-level area, unless further cross-regional curricula show a distinct route. The stored 12-role count is not used to choose the number.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Retain Personal Services Workers as the single student-facing group
alternatives_considered.reason: It is an ISCO occupational bucket, not an intelligible beauty/spa practice area, and mixes services without showing what learners actually specialize in.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Treat spa as only a place where other beauty services happen
alternatives_considered.reason: CIDESCO offers Spa Therapy as a standalone qualification with distinct training and assessment. The D088 taxonomy should distinguish spa therapy from salon facial/body/nail services while still allowing overlap where a treatment is genuinely shared.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Put make-up, nails and epilation under one catch-all finishing services group
alternatives_considered.reason: WorldSkills and CIDESCO describe these as separate technical service families with different knowledge, tools, contraindications and practice standards; combining them obscures the learner's actual specialization.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Add aromatherapy as a seventh area
alternatives_considered.reason: Aromatherapy appears as a distinct qualification but also as a modality within body/spa services. Current evidence is insufficient to establish a separate top-level D088 area rather than a technique or post-qualification focus.

residual_uncertainties: CIDESCO is a globally active professional education body but its course portfolio is not a universal occupational taxonomy; WorldSkills is a global vocational benchmark, while the detailed competency standards cited are UK-specific.

The term 'aesthetics' is used differently across jurisdictions. This recommendation limits it to non-medical cosmetic services; clinical/invasive procedures and protected titles require country-specific legal and professional review.
The existing D088 domain description is blank in the audit inventory. The specialization recommendation does not by itself repair the domain's full parent-scope definition or validate its 12 roles.
Canonical implementation remains pending specialization identifiers independent of ISCO and compatible seed/API support.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the excluded ISCO bucket with three candidate areas: Funeral Arrangement and Ceremony Direction; Mortuary Care, Embalming and Restorative Presentation; and Cemetery, Crematory and Disposition Operations. This is an internal synthesis informed by an international professional federation, employer-developed occupational standards and comparative funeral-service curricula; no source mandates these exact three labels/count. Do not treat country-specific licensing, burial/cremation law, or one culture's funeral practices as universal.
domains.count_rationale: source_reviewed_specialization_set_recommended

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Three is a minimal synthesis of the independently distinguishable funeral-direction, mortuary-care and disposition-facility functions found in global sector representation, occupational standards and comparative curricula. A separate grief-counselling specialization is not added: funeral professionals may support bereaved clients, but clinical counseling is a distinct regulated profession. A separate funeral-heritage group is also not added at this stage; heritage and cultural practices inform all branches and can be cross-cutting study topics.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep Personal Services Workers as the only student-facing group
alternatives_considered.reason: It is an ISCO classification family and gives learners no explanation of the distinct funeral, mortuary and disposition work areas.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Use Funeral Directing and Embalming as the only two areas
alternatives_considered.reason: This omits cemetery and crematory/disposition operations, which are recognized separately by FIAT-IFTA and ICCFA and appear in role/curriculum frameworks.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Add bereavement counselling or cultural heritage as separate areas
alternatives_considered.reason: Client support and funeral heritage are important, but current evidence treats these as cross-cutting responsibilities; independent specialization status and professional boundary require further international curriculum evidence. Clinical grief therapy remains outside funeral-service scope.

residual_uncertainties: Funeral customs and terminology vary substantially by culture and religion. The three areas are functional work clusters, not a prescription for any community's funeral practices.

Licensing and permitted handling of remains, embalming, cremation, cemetery operation and documentation are jurisdiction-specific. No U.S. or UK qualification or rule is represented as globally required.
The domain's four current role records remain unverified; the specialization count is not based on that count and does not approve any record.
Canonical implementation remains pending specialization identifiers independent of ISCO and compatible seed/API support.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the excluded ISCO bucket with four candidate areas: Companion Animal Care, Boarding and Shelter Services; Animal Grooming and Coat Care; Animal Training and Behaviour; and Zoological, Wildlife and Sanctuary Care. This is an internal synthesis of cross-organizational training/welfare standards and animal-care frameworks, not a prescribed four-part taxonomy. The domain's breadth and blank parent-scope description need correction/confirmation before canonical specialization IDs are applied. Breeding, livestock hoof-care and veterinary treatment should not be included under a generic area without separate parent-domain task evidence.
domains.count_rationale: source_reviewed_specialization_set_recommended

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Four candidates separate the service contexts substantiated by the sources while keeping shared foundations (welfare, safe handling, records and species knowledge) cross-cutting. Pet grooming is sufficiently technical to be a distinct area; behaviour/training has a separate competency standard; zoological and sanctuary care require taxon-specific husbandry; general companion care/boarding/shelter practice is the remaining service context. Animal breeding is not added because breeding may belong to animal science/production and GFAS specifically distinguishes sanctuary care from intentional breeding; verify any breeding role elsewhere. The stored 15-role count does not justify the count.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep Personal Services Workers as the sole student-facing subgroup
alternatives_considered.reason: It is a generic ISCO occupational bucket and conceals substantial differences between grooming, training, companion-care and zoo/sanctuary husbandry.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a separate area for every animal species or breed
alternatives_considered.reason: Species-specific knowledge is essential within animal care, but the reviewed standards support task and setting clusters, not a subgroup for every species/breed. Species knowledge should specialize each relevant path rather than fragment the top-level taxonomy.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Include veterinary care and animal breeding as D090 areas
alternatives_considered.reason: Veterinary practice is a distinct professional scope, while breeding/production can belong to animal science and production domains. The broad current role inventory is not evidence of fit; audit each role independently and link to other domains where supported.

residual_uncertainties: D090 has no current parent-domain scope description in the inventory. Its domain title spans companion pets and zoo/wildlife care, and the source role list also contains breeding, livestock and equine candidates. The parent scope must be refined before these candidate areas can be canonicalized.

AKC is U.S.-specific; zookeeper framework is European; GFAS is global but sanctuary-specific; IAABC standards are cross-organizational. Their combined evidence supports practice boundaries but does not substitute for cross-regional academic review.
No external academic sign-off has been obtained, and none of the 15 role mappings is approved by this recommendation.
Canonical implementation remains pending a clarified parent scope, specialization identifiers independent of ISCO and compatible seed/API support.

areas.label: Companion Animal Care, Boarding and Shelter Services
areas.boundary: Provide routine, safe, non-clinical care and welfare support to companion animals in home-care, boarding or rescue/shelter settings.
areas.source_support_claim: GFAS standards distinguish animal care from facility operations and apply to rescue/sanctuary settings; AKC grooming standards cover safe, humane care processes. Parent scope must be clarified to distinguish companion animals from wildlife/zoo settings.

evidence.title: National Core Professional Dog Grooming Educational Standards
evidence.locator: Framework states six educational domains: groomer safety; pet safety/humane treatment; sanitation; dog anatomy/physical characteristics; professional grooming practice; professionalism/business. Core practices include grooming methods by coat type, bathing/drying, safe handling, humane behavior management and client communication.
evidence.claim_supported: Dog grooming is a defined technical practice area distinct from general pet care and training, with species/coat knowledge, sanitation, safe handling and grooming techniques.
evidence.claim_limit: AKC is a U.S. national organization and the standards are dog-specific, not a global taxonomy for all animal grooming or proof of any role's D090 fit. Geographic scope: United States.

evidence.source_type: international animal sanctuary accreditation and care standards

evidence.claim_supported: Rescue, rehabilitation and sanctuary animal care form a distinct service context with animal-specific welfare and facility-operation requirements, separable from private pet grooming/boarding.
evidence.claim_limit: GFAS standards are voluntary and apply to sanctuary/rescue contexts; they are not a universal animal-care occupation taxonomy and do not establish role fit or a required subgroup count. Geographic scope: facilities worldwide.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the two excluded occupational buckets with four candidate road-driver/rider instruction areas: Car and Light-Vehicle Instruction; Motorcycle and Moped Rider Instruction; Commercial Goods-Vehicle Instruction; and Bus, Coach and Passenger-Vehicle Instruction. Do not include vessel steering under this road-driving taxonomy: maritime training is governed by a separate seafarer competency/certification regime and requires a separate parent-domain decision. This is a cross-source synthesis, not an externally prescribed four-area taxonomy, and it does not validate any role mapping.
domains.count_rationale: source_reviewed_specialization_set_recommended

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Four is a compact synthesis of the internationally distinguished vehicle types and independently evidenced training curricula. It avoids a separate top-level area for every licence subclass, endorsement, transmission type, fleet context or post-test programme. Vessel steering is excluded because it is a maritime competency regime under IMO's international STCW framework, not a road-driving specialization; if the parent domain intentionally covers maritime instruction, that activity needs a distinct, properly scoped parent-domain treatment rather than being hidden inside a road-driver area.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep the two ISCO-derived occupational groups as the student-facing specializations
alternatives_considered.reason: Teaching Professionals and Personal Service Workers are occupational classification groupings, not explanations of the different vehicle-specific knowledge and instruction contexts a learner would explore.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a separate subgroup for every licence class, endorsement, training stage, fleet setting or driving style
alternatives_considered.reason: These often represent jurisdiction-specific licensing subdivisions, delivery settings or course formats. Keep them as local variants or topics unless cross-regional discipline evidence shows a distinct specialization with different core learning requirements.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Include vessel steering instruction within road-driver/rider specializations
alternatives_considered.reason: UNECE road-traffic categories concern road vehicles, while IMO STCW sets distinct competence and certification standards for seafarers. Combining vessel steering with road-driver instruction would obscure different operating environments, competencies and regulatory authorities.

residual_uncertainties: The current D091 description spans road vehicles and vessels. The role-to-domain lane must independently establish whether the vessel steering instructor mapping should be removed, moved to a justified maritime domain, or retained only with a defensible explicit scope revision.

The cited detailed instructor standards are UK, Australian and U.S. national sources; UNECE supplies international road-vehicle categories but does not define instructor specializations. The four-area set is an evidence-backed internal synthesis, not a global consensus taxonomy or academic accreditation decision.
Licensing classes, commercial endorsements, instructor registration and legal authority are jurisdiction-specific and must be labelled as such in later enrichment.
Canonical implementation remains pending independent specialization identifiers and generator/API support.

disposition.label: rename/merge/split/add/remove specialization areas
disposition.reason: The review recommends a changed, renamed, merged, split, added, removed, or newly defined specialization set; this remains a recommendation, not a canonical edit.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the three ISCO-derived buckets with four candidate areas: Culinary Production and Kitchen Operations; Baking, Pastry and Confectionery; Food and Beverage Service; and Catering and Foodservice Operations Management. This is a compact internal synthesis of international occupational standards and comparative curricula, not a count prescribed by WorldSkills or an academic accreditor. Clarify the parent description to include management of commercial and institutional foodservice systems; do not infer that every catering role belongs in the management area.
domains.count_rationale: Four is the smallest set in this evidence that preserves distinct production, baking/pastry craft, guest-service, and systems-management competencies. Merging operations management into front-of-house service is rejected because comparative curricula teach logistics, staffing, procurement and cost control as distinct content. A separate group for each venue is rejected; bakery and pastry are combined. The count is not derived from role counts or ISCO codes.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Four is the smallest set in this evidence that preserves distinct production, baking/pastry craft, guest-service, and systems-management competencies. Merging operations management into front-of-house service is rejected because comparative curricula teach logistics, staffing, procurement and cost control as distinct content. A separate group for each venue is rejected; bakery and pastry are combined. The count is not derived from role counts or ISCO codes.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep the current ISCO-derived three visible groups
alternatives_considered.reason: They are occupational-code buckets, not coherent areas of study/practice, and combine distinct cooking, baking, service, and support functions.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Use only Culinary Production, Baking/Pastry, and Food and Beverage Service
alternatives_considered.reason: UPM, Porto, and UAB curricula establish operations-management content in menus, logistics, staffing, procurement, cost, quality and delivery that is not front-of-house service execution.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create one area per venue or population (hotel, hospital, school, airline, event, quick-service)
alternatives_considered.reason: Venues are applications of shared production/service/management competencies; the sources do not establish a distinct specialization for each setting.

residual_uncertainties: The four-part set is an internal cross-source synthesis, not a global consensus taxonomy or formal academic approval; additional cross-regional curriculum review may refine the boundaries.
Foodservice-management education sits in different faculties across countries; curriculum location does not alone determine the parent-domain boundary.
The raw legacy role library has 23 D092 rows, while the cleaned source and role-fit lane have 21. Confirm all downstream generation uses the cleaned source before any canonical role edit.
Canonical implementation awaits completion of the catalogue-wide specialization review and an independent specialization identifier/schema. No role-to-specialization link is approved here.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the excluded ISCO bucket with two candidate areas: Building and Commercial Electrical Installation; and Electrical Power Networks and Distribution. The international WorldSkills standard describes broad installation/maintenance practice across building and industrial environments, while CIGRE's global technical structure and separate network occupational standards distinguish transmission/distribution assets, cables, overhead lines and substations. This is a source-grounded synthesis, not an externally mandated two-part taxonomy. Keep industrial automation, electronics, and vehicle/marine/rail electrical systems outside the proposed specialization set unless role-task/domain-scope review proves a specific D093 fit; their presence in the legacy parent description or role library alone is not sufficient.
domains.count_rationale: Two is the smallest set supported by the current evidence that preserves the material boundary between premises installation/maintenance and electricity-network infrastructure. A single undifferentiated group would conceal the different operating environments and network equipment described by CIGRE and network occupational standards. More than two is not justified yet: the WorldSkills installation standard treats building automation, renewables and EV charging as installation content, while industrial automation is represented in distinct mechatronics/control standards and should not be imported merely because D093 currently has industrial electrician records.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Two is the smallest set supported by the current evidence that preserves the material boundary between premises installation/maintenance and electricity-network infrastructure. A single undifferentiated group would conceal the different operating environments and network equipment described by CIGRE and network occupational standards. More than two is not justified yet: the WorldSkills installation standard treats building automation, renewables and EV charging as installation content, while industrial automation is represented in distinct mechatronics/control standards and should not be imported merely because D093 currently has industrial electrician records.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Retain the single ISCO-74 subgroup
alternatives_considered.reason: It is a generic occupational classification bucket, not a meaningful student-facing area of specialization and it does not distinguish premises work from utility network infrastructure.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Use one broad electrical-installation specialization for all current D093 roles

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the two excluded ISCO buckets with four candidate areas: Electronic Hardware Design, Assembly and Embedded Systems; Electronics Installation, Testing and Maintenance; ICT and Communications Equipment Servicing; and Smart-Building and Connected-Systems Integration. This is a compact synthesis of WorldSkills occupational standards, ESCO task descriptions and the KNX/CEDIA smart-systems practice context. It is not an externally mandated taxonomy or approval of any role mapping. Clarify the root description so it describes the scope rather than implying that only repair-workshop servicing belongs.
domains.count_rationale: Four areas are the smallest proposed set that preserves the source-recognized electronics hardware/embedded, equipment lifecycle, ICT/communications servicing and connected building-systems work objects without creating one subgroup per device or employer sector. PCB production is grouped with electronics design/assembly; installation, testing and repair are grouped as one equipment lifecycle area; smart building integration is separated because its cross-system configuration and commissioning differ from servicing individual devices. The count is an internal synthesis, not a standard-setting body's prescribed number.

PCB production is grouped with electronics design/assembly; installation, testing and repair are grouped as one equipment lifecycle area; smart building integration is separated because its cross-system configuration and commissioning differ from servicing individual devices. The count is an internal synthesis, not a standard-setting body's prescribed number.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Expose the two ISCO-derived groups as-is

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create a separate subgroup for each device or sector (phones, ATMs, marine, railway, office equipment)

alternatives_considered.alternative: Merge smart-building integration into general electronics maintenance
alternatives_considered.reason: KNX and CEDIA describe cross-system design/configuration/integration and commissioning as a coherent practice, not merely repair of one electronic device.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Add broad industrial automation and vehicle/rail/marine electronics as separate D094 areas

residual_uncertainties: The four-area structure is a cross-source synthesis, not a globally ratified taxonomy or academic accreditation decision.
WorldSkills is an international occupational-skills standard; ESCO is a European classification whose occupation descriptions are corroborative rather than globally binding.
KNX describes its own open smart-building ecosystem, and CEDIA is an industry credential body; neither makes a vendor/platform credential universally required.
Some current role records may belong in adjacent domains when actual tasks are reviewed; this specialization recommendation does not validate them.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the five excluded ISCO buckets with three candidate areas: Passenger and Light-Commercial Vehicle Service and Repair; Heavy-Vehicle Service and Repair; and Vehicle Body Repair and Refinishing. The set is grounded in distinct international WorldSkills occupational standards and cross-checked against ASE's separate competency tracks. Keep narrower systems (brakes, tyres, engines, electrical systems) as subject/tool/competency themes within the relevant path unless stronger evidence shows a separate specialization. Do not expand the root to bicycles or rail vehicles; those are not motor vehicles in this domain's stated scope.
domains.count_rationale: Three is the smallest source-supported set that preserves the distinct light-vehicle, heavy-vehicle and collision/body/refinishing work contexts without creating one subgroup per component or shop task. Body repair and refinishing are combined as adjacent stages of the collision-repair lifecycle; the two vehicle service categories remain separate because the heavy-vehicle standard describes materially different vehicle systems and service demands. This is a synthesis, not a count prescribed by an accreditor.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Three is the smallest source-supported set that preserves the distinct light-vehicle, heavy-vehicle and collision/body/refinishing work contexts without creating one subgroup per component or shop task. Body repair and refinishing are combined as adjacent stages of the collision-repair lifecycle; the two vehicle service categories remain separate because the heavy-vehicle standard describes materially different vehicle systems and service demands. This is a synthesis, not a count prescribed by an accreditor.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Retain all five excluded ISCO-derived groups
alternatives_considered.reason: They classify occupations by broad code families rather than presenting coherent vehicle-repair specializations; several do not describe student learning areas.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create separate areas for brakes, tyres, engines, electrical systems and each repair component
alternatives_considered.reason: These are systems/competency lanes within vehicle service and repair; the evidence reviewed supports broader vehicle-context and collision-repair distinctions without subgroup proliferation.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Keep body repair and refinishing as two areas
alternatives_considered.reason: WorldSkills recognizes both crafts, but they form linked stages of collision repair and can be shown as themes within one student specialization; the available evidence does not require two top-level subgroup cards.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Include bicycles and rail vehicles under motor-vehicle repair
alternatives_considered.reason: Bicycles are not motor vehicles, and rail-vehicle technology has its own vehicle systems and maintenance context; the current parent title does not establish either as in-scope.

residual_uncertainties: The three-area set is a cross-source synthesis, not a globally ratified taxonomy or academic accreditation decision.
The WorldSkills standards provide international occupational benchmarks; ASE's framework is U.S.-specific and is corroborative only.

The canonical role audit must determine whether current D095 rows such as bicycle mechanic, rail/tramway technician, restoration technician and supervisor fit this parent domain at all; this specialization review intentionally does not decide those links.

EV/hybrid service, motorcycles and commercial fleet specialisms may merit later scoped treatment if the root-domain catalogue and source evidence establish distinct, coherent student areas; no such expansion is inferred from the three reviewed sources.

domains.recommendation_text: Replace the generic excluded ISCO bucket with three candidate areas: Welding and Joining; Metal Fabrication and Structural Assembly; and Forging and Blacksmithing. The proposed set separates controlled joining, preparation/assembly of metal products and structures, and hot-forging/hand- or machine-shaped metal craft. Treat processes/materials (MIG/MAG, TIG, arc, cutting, sheet metal, structural steel, aluminum, etc.) as themes/competencies within the appropriate area, not as separate subgroup cards. This is a source-based synthesis, not a globally mandated count.
domains.count_rationale: Three is the smallest proposed set that preserves the source-supported distinction between welding/joining, broader fabrication/assembly, and forging/blacksmithing while avoiding one subgroup per welding process, metal type or product sector. Welding and fabrication are related but not identical in the source frameworks; forging uses a distinct thermal shaping process and has a named craft/trade profile across several jurisdictions.

defensibility_and_rejected_alternatives.criteria_count_and_coverage: Three is the smallest proposed set that preserves the source-supported distinction between welding/joining, broader fabrication/assembly, and forging/blacksmithing while avoiding one subgroup per welding process, metal type or product sector. Welding and fabrication are related but not identical in the source frameworks; forging uses a distinct thermal shaping process and has a named craft/trade profile across several jurisdictions.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Expose the generic ISCO metal/machinery bucket as the only area
alternatives_considered.reason: It mixes unrelated occupations and does not tell students what metalworking practice they would learn.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Merge welding and all fabrication into one specialization
alternatives_considered.reason: Welding is a specific joining process family; fabrication also includes drawing interpretation, cutting, forming, fitting and assembly, and the international quality framework treats welding fabrication as a lifecycle rather than a synonym for welding.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Create separate areas for each welding process, metal, product or sector

domains.recommendation_text: The three-stage production model is strongly supported for the print-production scope. Keep graphic design and content creation distinct: design may supply print-ready work but is not itself pre-press/press/post-press production. Digital printing changes equipment/workflow but does not erase file preparation, press/output production, and post-press finishing functions.
Specific press technologies and bindery methods are themes/tools, not separate areas absent a distinct curriculum route.
